claims.text: Controlled sputter deposition can produce nanostructured non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy films.
Nanostructured FeMnNiGeSi films have a high density of grain boundaries.
Grain boundaries act as distributed heterogeneous nucleation sites during the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing grain-boundary density broadens the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing grain-boundary density reduces hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The baseline material has a relatively coarse microstructure and low grain-boundary density.
The baseline material exhibits a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Sputter deposition onto a substrate heated to around 500 degrees Celsius, with controlled rate and pressure, yields an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
A high film surface-to-volume ratio facilitates rapid heat exchange.
Grain boundaries lower local nucleation barriers for the magnetostructural phase change.
Distributed nucleation makes the transition more gradual and spatially broadened.
A gradual, spatially broadened transition reduces hysteresis under low-applied-field cycling.
Nanostructured films will show a smoother magnetization-versus-temperature response than the baseline.
Nanostructured films will show a less sharp calorimetric entropy change than the baseline.
Nanostructured films will exhibit less cycling hysteresis than the baseline.
The sharp baseline transition is caused by a uniform nucleation barrier in a coarse-grained, single-phase hexagonal state.
The predictions typically apply when film thickness is below the micrometer scale and substrate temperature permits substantial control of nucleation.
Very large-grained or overly amorphous films may not exhibit the predicted behavior.
Residual stress and unintended compositional variation may modify the effect attributed to grain-boundary density.

contradictions.description: The baseline is inconsistently defined as as-deposited thin films, bulk arc-melted ingots, or melt-spun ribbons. This makes it unclear whether the comparison isolates grain-boundary density, sample geometry, or fabrication route.

The experiment varies deposition parameters that can simultaneously alter grain size, texture, stress, and composition, while the falsification rule treats texture or stress overriding the trend as falsification rather than as a confounded test.
